title: Wanting more, until the grave
translation: Competing for more distracts you until you visit the graves. No, you will come to know! Again, no, you will come to know! If only you had the knowledge of certainty! You will see the Blaze, then see it with the eye of certainty. That day you will be asked about your pleasures.
body: **Zurtum al-maqābir**: Muqātil and al-Kalbī report two Quraysh clans **counting their dead** in graveyards to settle a boast; Ibn Kathir reads “visit” as **dying**. On gifts and what they demand, Luther’s **Small Catechism**: “I must thank Him, praise Him, serve Him and obey Him.”
question: “Until you visit the graves”: a literal contest counting the dead, or simply a figure for dying?
